title: 3D Rendering in Chicago, IL: Product and Packaging | 22 Signals
description: 3D rendering for Chicago manufacturers, food brands and developers: photoreal product, packaging, booth and interior visuals, made from CAD or sketches.
h1: 3D rendering for Chicago products, packaging and spaces
intro: We provide 3D rendering for Chicago companies that need photoreal visuals before, or instead of, a photo shoot: product renders, packaging, campaign images, trade show booths, interiors and 3D models for web and ads. It suits manufacturers, food and consumer brands, furniture and fixture makers, and real estate teams who want images ready for sales, retail and launch dates.

sections.h: Why renders beat photo shoots more often than you think
p: A photo shoot needs the finished product, a studio, a stylist and the right weather for anything outdoors, which in Chicago rules out a good part of the year. A render needs a CAD file or a good set of reference photos. Once the model exists, you can show every color, size and pack variant, from any angle, and update it when the label changes.

That is the case for 3D rendering. Chicago food brands, equipment makers and consumer goods companies often sell with renders first: retailer presentations, distributor catalogs, e-commerce listings and trade show graphics, often months before production starts.

Interior and architectural visualization for offices, showrooms, restaurants and residential projects.

p: A render used in a retailer pitch or a catalog has to be right. We match colors to your brand values, check dimensions against your drawings, and get labels and regulatory panel layouts from your design team rather than guessing. Every render goes through review rounds on a shared link, and your team signs off before anything is final.
If you use renders on pack or in ads, the usual advertising rules still apply: the product has to look like the product. We keep renders honest to what will actually ship.

sections.h: What good 3D rendering, Chicago style, looks like in a line review
p: Retail line reviews and distributor meetings are where renders earn their money. A buyer at a grocery chain sees your new pack on a virtual shelf next to the competition. A distributor rep scrolls through every finish of a fixture on a tablet. An engineer at a trade show rotates a 3D model of a pump to see the inlet.

In each case the images need to load fast, look consistent across the range and match what will ship. We set a lighting and camera standard for your whole catalog, so a render made next year sits cleanly beside one made this year.

sections.h: One team for the render and what comes after
p: Most rendering studios hand you images and stop there. We cover AI, cloud and data, marketing, and video, animation and 3D in one team, so the same models can become a product animation, a paid social campaign, an e-commerce page or a configurator on your site. Over $1.5 million in projects managed has taught us that the handoffs between vendors are where launches slip. With one Signal Lead, there are fewer handoffs.

We deliver 3D rendering for Chicago clients remotely, and no one needs to ship samples unless a material is hard to match from photos. Reviews run on video at times that suit your team, and each round closes with a written list of changes. For trade show deadlines and retail line reviews, we plan backwards from the date and write the schedule down.

faqs.q: What files do you need for 3D rendering?
faqs.a: CAD files such as STEP or SolidWorks exports give the most accurate result, and most Chicago manufacturers already have them. If you do not, we can model from technical drawings, sketches or a set of reference photos with measurements. For packaging we need the dieline and the artwork files from your design team.

Often, yes, especially for e-commerce, catalogs, packaging pitches and products that do not exist yet. Renders let you show every variant without a shoot. For lifestyle images with people, some brands still mix in photography. We help you decide where renders do the job and where a real shoot is still worth it.

faqs.q: Do you render trade show booths for McCormick Place?
faqs.a: Yes. We render booth concepts so you can review the layout, graphics and product placement before the stand is built, and we produce the product hero images that go on the booth graphics. Show dates do not move, so we plan backwards from the show and agree the schedule in writing.

faqs.q: Do you need to visit our site in Chicago?
faqs.a: Usually not. Rendering works from files and photos, so the whole job runs remotely, with reviews on video. If a material is hard to judge from photos, you can ship a sample. For interiors, measured drawings and photos of the space are normally enough.

faqs.q: Can the same 3D models be used for animation?
faqs.a: Yes, and that is one of the main reasons to start with renders. Once a product is modeled, we can animate it for explainers, trade show loops and ads, or put it on your website as an interactive 3D view. Our video and animation team works from the same files.

faqs.q: Can you do architectural renders for Chicago real estate?
faqs.a: Yes. We produce interior and exterior visualization for offices, showrooms, restaurants and residential projects, from floor plans and design references. For Chicago developers and landlords repositioning older office buildings, renders help pre-lease or pre-sell space before the fit-out is finished.

faqs.q: How many renders do we need for a product launch?
faqs.a: Fewer than most brands expect. A typical launch set is a hero image, a few angles, a detail or cutaway shot and one lifestyle scene, plus variants. For 3D rendering, Chicago food and consumer brands also add shelf and case-pack views for retail buyers. We plan the set around where each image will appear, so nothing is made that nobody uses.
